subject: Evidence escrow & exchange process for AuditBridge integration
messages:
From: Maya R. <maya@auditbridge.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Cc: securityops@auditbridge.com
Date: 2026-12-05T08:07:00-08:00
Subject: Initial: evidence escrow & exchange process for AuditBridge integration

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Our GRC engineering team is moving ahead with the AuditBridge <> Redwood integration and we need to lock down how sensitive compliance artifacts (SOC2 snapshots, pen-test deliverables, signed attestations) will be exchanged and stored for evidence ingestion. A couple of requirements on our side:

- We need read-only, time-limited access to artifact snapshots (30-90 day TTL) for ingestion into our evidence store.
- Pen-test artifacts must be transferred via an auditable, checksum-verified channel; if you use a third-party escrow service we need the escrow manifest and chain-of-custody.
- We support S3 presigned URLs, SFTP, and mock DMS connectors; please advise what Redwood recommends for short-lived access.
- Please include a sample manifest and any legal docs (DPA / escrow terms) you expect partners to sign.

Can you share a one-pager describing the end-to-end flow and a manifest template? We'd like to review and schedule a technical handoff next week.

(attachment: auditbridge_integration_req.pdf)

Best,
Maya R.
Partnerships Lead — AuditBridge
maya@auditbridge.com

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Maya R. <maya@auditbridge.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-05T10:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial: evidence escrow & exchange process for AuditBridge integration

Hi Maya — thanks, this is exactly the right time to align. High-level proposal below; attaching a manifest template and a short process one-pager so your engineers/legal folks have concrete artifacts to review.

Proposed evidence escrow & exchange workflow (summary):
1) Snapshot collection: Redwood will create a read-only snapshot bundle (tar.gz) containing SOC2 artifact exports, configuration manifests, and a signed attestation.
2) Integrity: Each bundle will include a SHA256 manifest (artifact path, size, hash, signer).
3) Transfer & storage: Options we support — a) S3 presigned URL with 72-hour TTL (preferred), b) temporary SFTP account with key-based auth, c) upload to partner-managed GRC connector.
4) Escrow for pen-test artifacts: For penetration test deliverables we will route the bundle to a third-party escrow (we typically use RedlineSec for escrow custody) and provide AuditBridge with the escrow manifest + signed chain-of-custody.
5) Retention & access: Default retention 180 days (we can set 30/90 on a per-account basis). Short-lived credentials only; no long-term keys in the manifest.
6) Legal: We require a simple escrow addendum + DPA signature before we release pen-test artifacts.

Action items
- I attached a manifest template (redwood_evidence_manifest_template.csv) and a one-pager (escrow_process_onepager.pdf).
- Please confirm preferred transport (S3 presigned vs SFTP) and desired retention TTL.
- If AuditBridge requires a third-party escrow auditor or on-record custodian, let us know and we'll route accordingly.

We can do a tech handoff Wed/Thu next week; let me know what works.

Attachments: redwood_evidence_manifest_template.csv, escrow_process_onepager.pdf

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Strategic Partnerships, Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.com
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Maya R. <maya@auditbridge.com>, jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-05T13:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial: evidence escrow & exchange process for AuditBridge integration

Maya — quick technical notes from engineering:

- Pref S3 presigned URL flow: presigned POST/PUT with ACL private, object-level SSE (AES256) is straightforward and reduces operational friction. TTLs we can set between 24h–14d; typical recommendation 72h.
- SFTP: we can provision ephemeral keys for partners, but SFTP requires support windows and monitoring; acceptable if your ops team prefers it.
- Hashing & manifest: manifest must include SHA256 for every file; we publish a signed manifest (ECDSA) so AuditBridge can verify signature provenance.
- Pen-test artifacts: For chaining custody we'll include a notarized checksum file (redlinesec_artifact_checksums.txt) and a signed attestation file (attestation.json.sig). RedlineSec will push directly to escrow with a reference URL.

Security constraints:
- No archive will contain plaintext secrets or private keys.
- We will not deliver raw logs containing PII without an approved DPA and scoping.

If AuditBridge confirms S3 presigned, we'll provision a test bucket and share a sample presign flow for QA.

-Vivek
Sr. Partner Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: RedlineSec <alerts@redlinesec.io>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com, Maya R. <maya@auditbridge.com>
Date: 2026-12-06T09:24:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial: evidence escrow & exchange process for AuditBridge integration

Hi all — RedlineSec here. We will act as the evidence escrow for the upcoming pen-test artifacts. Planned deliverables and timing below: 

- Deliverables: redlinesec_report_summary.pdf, redlinesec_artifact_checksums.txt (SHA256), and chain-of-custody record (COC_20261206.pdf).
- Transfer method: we will POST signed bundles to your escrow endpoint (S3 presigned URL preferred). Each bundle will include a timestamped manifest and an ECDSA signature verifying origin.
- Timeline: initial artifact bundle available 2026-12-10; full report + raw artifacts by 2026-12-14 (subject to DPA clearance).

On 2026-12-05 Jasmine wrote:
> Proposed evidence escrow & exchange workflow (summary):
> 1) Snapshot collection: Redwood will create a read-only snapshot bundle (tar.gz) containing SOC2 artifact exports...

We will coordinate sign-off with Redwood security (Neha) to ensure the chain-of-custody meets AuditBridge ingestion requirements.

Regards,
RedlineSec Escrow Team
alerts@redlinesec.io

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Maya R. <maya@auditbridge.com>, jasmine_liu@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-07T15:43:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial: evidence escrow & exchange process for AuditBridge integration — security sign-off & next steps

Hi Maya / team — I reviewed the flow and we can support the escrow model as described with the following security checklist and preconditions: 

Mandatory preconditions (must be in place before pen-test artifacts are released):
- Signed DPA (we'll share draft) and a simple escrow addendum specifying custody responsibilities. (attachment: dpa_draft_redwood.pdf)
- All transfer bundles include a SHA256 manifest and an ECDSA signature; the signature public key will be registered to AuditBridge.
- Pen-test artifacts will be delivered via S3 presigned URL with server-side encryption (AES256). If AuditBridge mandates SFTP, we will provision ephemeral keys for your ops users.
- Retention window: default 180 days. If AuditBridge requires a shorter TTL (30/90 days), we will accommodate at onboarding but need written agreement.
- No PII/production secrets in delivered artifacts without a scoped exception documented in the DPA.

Next steps & owners:
- Jasmine: share the DPA draft and process one-pager to AuditBridge legal (today).
- Maya: confirm transport preference (S3 presigned preferred) and desired TTL (30/90/180).
- Vivek: provision a test bucket and sample presign flow for AuditBridge QA (target: 2026-12-09).
- RedlineSec: provide the preliminary checksum bundle and expected delivery dates (acknowledged).

If all parties agree, let's lock a 30-minute technical handoff on 2026-12-09 or 12-10. I can join to confirm the signature verification and manifest parsing.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Dir., Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
